facts.text: A Collision Warning System (CWS) only alerts the operator to a nearby object, whereas a Collision Avoidance System (CAS) also acts on the machine by slowing or stopping it.
facts.quote: A Collision Warning System (CWS) only alerts the operator to a nearby object, while a Collision Avoidance System (CAS) also acts on the machine, slowing or stopping it.

facts.text: The booklet's Collision Mitigation System is a Collision Avoidance System (CAS) in the glossary's vocabulary.
facts.quote: The booklet's Collision Mitigation System is a CAS in this vocabulary.

facts.text: Standards and researchers use CWS/CAS terminology or the umbrella term CXS for both collision warning and collision avoidance systems.
facts.quote: Standards and researchers write CWS/CAS, or use the umbrella term CXS for both [Chapters 1, 3].

facts.text: ISO 21815-1 covers detection, operator warning, automatic intervention and test procedures for both collision warning and collision avoidance systems.
facts.quote: ISO 21815-1 covers detection, operator warning, automatic intervention and test procedures for both kinds [Chapter 3].

facts.text: The manufacturer's current product is a collision warning system, while the new product is a collision avoidance system.
facts.quote: The manufacturer's current product is a warning system; the new one is an avoidance system

facts.text: The industry is transitioning from collision warning systems to collision avoidance systems.
facts.quote: The manufacturer's current product is a warning system; the new one is an avoidance system, and the industry is in the same transition.

facts.text: A NIOSH review of 97 haul-truck collision-system cases from 2000 to 2020 found that 37% were warning systems and only 10% were avoidance systems.
facts.quote: A NIOSH review of 97 haul-truck collision-system cases from 2000 to 2020 found 37% were warning systems and only 10% avoidance systems

facts.text: Most haul-truck collision-system cases in the NIOSH review covering 97 cases from 2000 to 2020 were at low technology-readiness levels.
facts.quote: A NIOSH review of 97 haul-truck collision-system cases from 2000 to 2020 found 37% were warning systems and only 10% avoidance systems, most at low technology-readiness levels [Chapter 8].

facts.text: Transitioning from collision warning to collision avoidance changes the safety problem: a wrong warning causes annoyance, while a wrong intervention commands a machine weighing tens or hundreds of tons to stop.
facts.quote: The step changes the safety problem: a wrong warning costs annoyance, while a wrong intervention is a command that stops a machine weighing tens or hundreds of tons [Chapter 4].

facts.text: The collision mitigation validation plan can reuse knowledge from the existing warning system about sensors, scenarios and false-alarm history.
facts.quote: The plan can reuse much of what the warning system taught (sensors, scenarios, false-alarm history)

facts.text: The collision mitigation validation plan must add new evidence for everything after the brake command because the existing warning system never exercised that part of the function.
facts.quote: must add new evidence for everything after the brake command, which the warning system never exercised [Chapters 1, 7].
